clue.text: Shakespearean question of identity — could be Viola's — I wish!

indicators.note: the letters of the following words could be arranged into something else, so they are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive 's supplying its S here
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a famous line of Shakespeare could have been spoken by Viola, if only.
explanation.walkthrough: The song in The Two Gentlemen of Verona asks who this woman is; Viola, from Twelfth Night, is a red herring. The S of Viola's counts as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The title line of a song in The Two Gentlemen of Verona is a question asking a lady's identity.

clue.text: Crazy poet's two novels fool many, completely circulating with blonde dumbed down?

indicators.note: something crazy is wild and disordered, so the letters that follow are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, its S counted
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
completely means wholly, entirely

explanation.surface: A deranged poet's pair of novels hoodwinks the public with a ditzy blonde heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circulating' is a second signal for the mixing. The famous Oliver Goldsmith song from The Vicar of Wakefield begins with these words; the definition playfully reads the line as a pretty woman acting foolishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldsmith's line pictures a beautiful woman who behaves foolishly, jokingly rendered as a blonde who has been dumbed down.

clue.text: European agreements on board

parts.note: oui is the French word for yes
ja is the German word for yes

explanation.surface: Continental nations sign deals while on a committee.
explanation.walkthrough: The board for spirit messages is named from French and German words for yes; 'board' looks like a committee but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A planchette-and-letters board used in séances is called by this name.

clue.text: King going in to be stertorous, having left tube

indicators.note: the king's letter goes in to the middle of the snoring word

parts.note: stertorous means breathing noisily, so to be stertorous is to snore
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch begins snoring loudly after his breathing tube is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimmer's breathing tube is a common piece of diving kit.

clue.text: One bad summer puts one in prison

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: bad here signals the letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreadful summer sends someone to jail.
explanation.definitionFit: To immure someone is to wall them up or confine them, as in a jail.

clue.text: Dress up among struggles for basic facts

indicators.note: the reversed dress word sits among the letters of the struggles word

parts.note: vies means competes or struggles

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: tire is an old word meaning to dress or attire

explanation.surface: Getting dressed up is a struggle that reveals fundamental truths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress up' reads like getting smartened up, but 'up' reverses the dress word in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Verities are truths, the fundamental facts of a matter.

clue.text: Well protected with forelimbs on child (male) and choppers

parts.note: having arms, the forelimbs, is being armed
a tot is a small child
he is the male pronoun
choppers is slang for teeth

explanation.surface: A heavily defended figure has arms, a little boy, and big teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone carrying many weapons, hence very well protected.

clue.text: See 1
Farewell letters of ancient doctor (retired), one sent from Verona to 1 across's girl?

definitions.text: one sent from Verona to 1 across's girl?

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are taken and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: retired means going back, so the doctor abbreviation is turned round

explanation.surface: An old physician, now retired, sends a goodbye letter.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Two Gentlemen of Verona, Valentine woos Silvia, the girl of 1 across, so a token from him punningly names a lover's card.
explanation.definitionFit: A love card sent on 14 February bears the name of the Verona gentleman who courted Silvia.

clue.text: Italian city with fountain like this

parts.note: the Trevi is the famous fountain in Rome
so means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: An Italian town boasts a fountain built in this style.
explanation.definitionFit: Treviso is a city in the Veneto region of northern Italy.

clue.text: Instrument forming border between graduates

indicators.note: the border word goes between the two degree abbreviations

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts graduate
BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A musical instrument forms a dividing line between two university alumni.
explanation.definitionFit: A marimba is a percussion instrument like a large xylophone.

clue.text: What the pig said to the Queen about lieutenant on a ship

indicators.note: the pig's noise goes about, or around, the lieutenant and a

parts.note: oink is the sound a pig makes
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A farmyard pig addresses the monarch about a naval officer aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanker carrying petroleum is a type of cargo ship.

clue.text: Fox that's providing final resource 1down 7

parts.note: tod is an old dialect word for a fox
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A fox offers the last resort in Goldsmith's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Goldsmith's poem ends that the only art for the fallen woman is to die. TOD is a dialect word for fox.
explanation.definitionFit: In Goldsmith's song the sole remedy left for the woman's shame is death.

clue.text: Bar — don't spend!

definitions.meaning: ... as a preposition means except, as does bar
an instruction to keep money rather than use it

explanation.definitionFit: Save means except, like bar, and also means to keep money unspent.

clue.text: Defy without 'aving been silenced or driven from hiding

indicators.note: without means outside, so the defy word goes around the other

parts.note: to flout a rule is to defy it
hushed means silenced; the dropped H of 'aving tells us to drop the H too

explanation.surface: Someone resisted being quietened, or was forced out of a hiding place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aving mimics a Cockney dropped H, so HUSHED loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Game or fugitives flushed out are forced to leave cover.

clue.text: Reputation on feet?

definitions.meaning: one's ... is one's status or reputation

explanation.definitionFit: Standing means status in society and also being upright on one's feet.

clue.text: Fellow who can spell: after he's died, remove all traces

indicators.note: the speller comes after the death abbreviation

parts.note: ob., obiit, is Latin for he died, seen on gravestones
a literate is a person able to read and write

explanation.surface: A good speller is commemorated after death, then erased from memory.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to destroy utterly, wiping out every trace.

clue.text: Bend under water, perhaps, to judge right deed

parts.note: a ref, referee, is a judge in sport
an act is a deed

explanation.surface: A referee rules on a good deed done underwater.
explanation.definitionFit: Light refracts, or bends, as it passes into water.

clue.text: Country of splendid wickedness but topped coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: A1, written AI, means excellent or splendid
sin is wickedness

indicators.note: topped means the head, the first letter, is cut off

explanation.surface: A nation of glorious sin is nonetheless being brought down.
explanation.walkthrough: Splendid as A1 is a crossword convention, with the figure 1 written as the letter I. The whole charade is turned by 'coming up', since this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a country in North Africa.

clue.text: Half a farewell feature

indicators.note: half of the farewell word is kept, its first half

parts.note: ...-... is an old toast and farewell

explanation.surface: Half a goodbye is all you get from someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The chin is a feature of the face.

clue.text: Girl from Welshpool went away

indicators.note: the name comes from inside the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A young woman from a Welsh town left.
explanation.walkthrough: Welshpool is a town in mid Wales, fitting a Welsh name.
explanation.definitionFit: Olwen is a Welsh girl's name, from the legend of Culhwch and Olwen.

clue.text: Marvellous princess missing home gets endless criticism

indicators.note: the princess word goes without the home word

parts.note: an infanta is a Spanish or Portuguese princess
in means at home

indicators.note: the criticism word loses its final letter

parts.note: stick means harsh criticism

explanation.surface: A homeless princess is subjected to constant marvelling criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: INFANTA minus IN leaves FANTA; STICK minus its end leaves STIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic means wonderful or marvellous.

clue.text: Caucasian in blazer initially

indicators.note: the people's name sits inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A man from the Caucasus is wearing a blazer at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letter signal, but the letters run across both words.
explanation.definitionFit: An Azeri is a native of Azerbaijan in the Caucasus.

clue.text: English politician put in old European currency for Honduran

indicators.note: the English and politician letters are put in the currency

parts.note: the lira was Italy's currency before the euro
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A British MP is installed among old Italian money for a Central American.
explanation.definitionFit: The lempira is the monetary unit of Honduras.

clue.text: Ursa senior holding young shrub first

indicators.note: the senior abbreviation holds the other letters

parts.note: Hebe is the goddess of youth and also an evergreen shrub
A is first, as in grade A

explanation.surface: The Great Bear's elder holds a young bush ahead of others.
explanation.walkthrough: HEBE does double duty in the sense only: the goddess of youth and a shrub name. 'Ursa' is Latin for a female bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa is the Latin feminine word for a bear, as in the constellations.

clue.text: Like an incubus, not far from taking this arm off

parts.note: nigh means near, not far from

indicators.note: off signals the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Losing an arm close by would be truly terrifying.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus is an evil spirit or bad dream, so something like one is frightening.
